According to the Turkish newspaper Hürriyet, Turkey has resold its Russian S-400 long-range surface-to-air missile (SAM) systems to a Gulf country, possibly the United Arab Emirates or Qatar, in exchange for the United States agreeing to lift sanctions on Ankara and allow Turkey to rejoin the F-35 fighter program.
Both countries are looking to strengthen their air defense capabilities amid heightened regional tensions caused by the U.S.-Iran war. Qatar, in particular, has previously been reported to be interested in acquiring the Russian S-400 system.

The EU Parliament has voted to back new rules for return hubs outside Europe. This allows faster returns of rejected asylum seekers and irregular migrants to third countries, speeding up deportations and strengthening border management.
